cases.name: request-key-collision
cases.reason: two entries resolve to one request key (§5.1 step 6)

cases.name: request-key-declared-mismatch
cases.reason: a stored key that does not recompute from its own parts (CF6-5)

cases.name: policy-header-subset-unsorted
cases.reason: the declared header subset must be strictly ascending

cases.name: policy-header-subset-credential
cases.reason: a credential-bearing header must not key a sealed corpus (CF6-1)

cases.name: miss-policy-absent
cases.reason: fail-closed is non-negotiable, so the miss response is required (§4.4)

cases.name: miss-policy-redirect
cases.reason: a redirect miss points outside the sealed world (CF6-7)

cases.name: synthetic-claims-capture
cases.reason: a synthetic corpus that claims capture provenance is false by construction (CF6-8)

cases.name: entry-origin-undeclared
cases.reason: every entry origin must be declared in corpus.origins

cases.name: corpus-body-digest-mismatch
cases.reason: the record seals fine; the corpus does not materialize as it describes (§5.1 step 6)

cases.name: captured-provenance-unprovable
cases.reason: seals fine and is labeled a declaration; fidelity is never checked as a fact (§4.4)

cases.name: corpus-injected-instruction
cases.reason: seals fine and is served verbatim as data; nothing here interprets it (§8)
